newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Thursday due to overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 19,640 yuan ($2,366) per tonne, losing 60 yuan. It opened at 19,650 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 19,660 and a low of 19,550.
October fell 120 to 19,740 yuan, November 120 to 19,630, December 20 to 19,600, February 50 to 19,650, March 20 to 19,700 and April 110 to 19,690.
Combined volume fell to 37,800 tonnes from 45,280.
Copper opened lower and fell further before short-covering pushed contracts off lows later in the session. Later-maturing contracts found support above 19,500 yuan.
"Panic selling did not emerge because most investors believe copper on the LME is still consolidating despite overnight losses," one trader said.
But traders said a bearish atmosphere dominated the metal market following the breaching of the 20,000 yuan level a few days ago.
